title: $35 Million on Paper. $1.13 Million in Reality.

lines.say: Thirty-five million dollars. That's how much Martin Shkreli told people his hedge fund managed.
lines.show: $35 million. That's how much Martin Shkreli told people his hedge fund managed.

lines.say: A federal judge wrote that the fund never had more than about one point one three million at one time.
lines.show: A federal judge wrote that the fund never had more than about $1.13 million at one time.

lines.say: One bad trade in twenty eleven cost Merrill Lynch more than seven million dollars. His reports to investors kept showing positive returns.
lines.show: One bad trade in 2011 cost Merrill Lynch more than $7 million. His reports to investors kept showing positive returns.

lines.say: In twenty seventeen, a jury convicted him of securities fraud. Sentence: seven years. Not for the seven-hundred-fifty-dollar pill.
lines.show: In 2017, a jury convicted him of securities fraud. Sentence: 7 years. Not for the $750 pill.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
